research_question: Does one fixed five-bin Beta-binomial calibration of the existing consensus candidate score, fitted only on targets 201..600 and frozen for targets 601..1250, improve candidate main-number inclusion probability forecasts over the exact uniform 6/45 marginal baseline under Brier score and log loss?
novelty_statement: Prior candidate-recall work evaluated top-k capture counts, while E045/E048-E071 evaluated three-line portfolio hit metrics or distinct lagged feature families. E072 tests a different question: whether the full 45-number consensus score can be converted into calibrated marginal inclusion probabilities that improve proper scoring rules on a chronologically later holdout. One fixed score, one fixed five-bin estimator, one fixed train/test split, no variants, no parameter search. This is a new calibration research axis, not a claim of independent sample or portfolio readiness.
training_cutoff_rule: For each target t, compute the consensus score for each number using only draws 1..t-1. Fit quintile cutpoints and Beta-binomial bin probabilities using only candidate labels from training targets 201..600. Freeze all calibration parameters before evaluating targets 601..1250; evaluation outcomes never update cutpoints or probabilities.
score_definition: mean(recent30_z, gap_z, momentum_z, balanced_z, contrarian_z), exactly matching the frozen candidate_recall_v1.py feature implementation

calibration.binning: nearest-rank empirical quintiles of the 18,000 training candidate scores; cutpoint index ceil(k*N/5)-1 for k=1..4
calibration.tie_rule: bisect_right; a score equal to a cutpoint enters the higher bin
calibration.expected_six_normalization: For each evaluation target, add a single common logit intercept to the 45 raw probabilities by bisection until their sum is exactly six; no outcome information is used.

random_comparator.method: For each evaluation target, randomly permute the 45 normalized model probabilities over the 45 number labels, preserving the complete probability multiset and six-probability sum.

uniform_baseline.method: Exact marginal main-number inclusion probability 6/45 for each of the 45 numbers.

inference.comparison: paired per-target model loss minus exact uniform-baseline loss
inference.ci: two-sided percentile moving-block bootstrap; 4,000 replicates; 50-target blocks; sample 13 blocks and truncate to the original 650 targets
inference.promotion_rule: Both Bonferroni-adjusted 97.5% two-sided CI upper bounds for model-minus-uniform Brier and log loss must be strictly below zero. Random-permutation results are reported as an executed rank-randomization control.

strict_portfolio_policy.reason: Candidate probability calibration is not a three-line portfolio evaluation and cannot qualify STRICT_PASS_READY, even if its own calibration gate passes.
